title: Deleting a user keeps their articles with a null author but deletes their comments.
content:
articles.author_id is a nullable foreign key with ondelete SET NULL, while commentaries.author_id, favorites and follower rows use ondelete CASCADE. Code that reads article.author must tolerate articles whose author row is gone.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

title: Article lists default to 20 items with limit/offset paging and no upper bound on limit.
content:
DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET is 0; limit is validated only with ge=1 and offset with ge=0, both in the schema and in get_articles_filters. A client can request any large limit.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:8

title: Authentication failures return HTTP 403, not 401.
content:
A wrong token prefix, an undecodable or malformed token, and a token for a user that no longer exists all raise HTTPException with status 403. A missing header keeps the status of the underlying APIKeyHeader error but with the AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED message.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:90

title: The Authorization header must use the prefix "Token" instead of "Bearer".
content:
_get_authorization_header splits the header on a space and compares the prefix with settings.jwt_token_prefix, which defaults to "Token". Clients sending "Bearer <jwt>" are rejected.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

title: Only the author may update or delete an article, checked by comparing usernames.
content:
check_user_can_modify_article compares article.author.username with the current user's username, and the update and delete routes depend on check_article_modification_permissions, which raises 403. There is no admin or role override.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
content:
security.py builds CryptContext(schemes=["bcrypt"], deprecated="auto") and uses it for both hashing and verification. Switching scheme would break verification of stored hashes unless both schemes are listed.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

title: API models serialize snake_case fields as camelCase JSON via an alias generator.
content:
RWModel sets alias_generator = convert_field_to_camel_case and allow_population_by_field_name = True, so fields like created_at appear as createdAt. Renaming a Python field changes the public JSON key.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

title: The asyncpg connection pool defaults to a fixed size of 10 (min equals max).
content:
AppSettings sets max_connection_count and min_connection_count both to 10, and connect_to_db passes them as min_size and max_size to asyncpg.create_pool. Ten connections are opened at startup and the pool never grows beyond that.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:23

title: Creating an article whose title slugifies to an existing slug is rejected with HTTP 400.
content:
create_new_article computes the slug, calls check_article_exists, and raises ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS with status 400 if found. No suffix or random component is added to make slugs unique.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65

title: Access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm using the app secret key.
content:
create_jwt_token encodes with algorithm=ALGORITHM and get_username_from_token decodes with algorithms=[ALGORITHM], where ALGORITHM is HS256. The same secret_key signs and verifies, so any service that verifies tokens must hold the signing secret.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

title: Access tokens expire one week after issue and there is no refresh token.
content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7 and create_access_token_for_user passes it as expires_delta. No refresh or revocation mechanism exists; a new token is issued on login, register, get-current-user and update-current-user.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

title: The token identifies the user by username, not by numeric id.
content:
The token payload is JWTUser(username=user.username), and the auth dependency loads the user with get_user_by_username. Changing a username therefore invalidates existing tokens, which is why update-current-user returns a fresh token.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

title: A separately stored per-user salt is prepended to the password before bcrypt hashing.
content:
change_password generates a salt with bcrypt.gensalt, stores it in the salt column, and hashes salt + password. check_password must concatenate in the same order, so the salt column and its ordering are part of the stored-password format.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

title: Updating an article's title regenerates its slug, so its URL changes.
content:
update_article_by_slug recomputes the slug from article_update.title when a title is given and passes it to update_article. Unlike create, this path does not call check_article_exists first.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:100

title: An article slug is derived from its title with slugify and is the article's public identifier.
content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title). Routes address articles and their comments by /{slug}, and the articles.slug column is unique.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19

title: Login returns the same 400 error for an unknown email and for a wrong password.
content:
The login route builds one wrong_login_error with INCORRECT_LOGIN_INPUT and raises it both when get_user_by_email finds no user and when check_password fails. Login is by email, not username.
Source: app/app/api/routes/authentication.py:30

title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL trigger, not by application code.
content:
The migration creates the plpgsql function update_updated_at_column, which sets NEW.updated_at = now(), and attaches BEFORE UPDATE triggers to users, articles and commentaries. Removing the trigger would silently stop updated_at from changing.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27
